rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while encouraging all eight compounds to elute. An intermediate temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.
Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity of the sole unresolved pair. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving room for a shallower gradient if needed.

Make the gradient modestly shallower at the favorable temperature to lift the first pair above R = 1.5. The last peak currently elutes well before 10 minutes, leaving ample time margin to reach CRF 1.0.

The maximum CRF is already secured by injection 3. Test an intermediate gradient slope to shorten retention while aiming to keep the first pair above R = 1.5; the new endpoint remains comfortably above the last peak’s estimated elution composition.

Raise the gradient window by 0.05 while preserving the slope of injection 4 to test whether retention can be shortened without losing full resolution. The first peaks were well retained, but their separation remains the key constraint.

Restore the lower starting organic fraction and test a slope just steeper than injection 4, aiming to retain full resolution with slightly earlier elution. The endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution composition of about 0.57.

Test a slightly steeper slope to locate the shortest fully resolved boundary between injections 6 and 2. This should shorten retention, though the first pair may fall just below R = 1.5; injection 6 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a slope between injections 6 and 7, targeting first-pair resolution just above 1.5. The last compound will likely elute shortly into the final hold, so this also tests whether the lower endpoint preserves the time advantage.

With CRF 1.0 secured, test the low-temperature selectivity regime for a possible alternative separation of the first pair. The steeper, broad gradient limits the retention-time increase expected on cooling.

Test whether modest warming separates the late three-peak cluster while retaining the favorable early-pair selectivity seen at 25 C. A shallower gradient should help spread that cluster, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Test an intermediate temperature to separate the late cluster, while a higher starting organic fraction and shorter gradient reduce retention. This probes whether shifting the gradient window also improves the early pair’s selectivity in the cooler regime.

Reduce the slope at 35 C to improve the early pair while preserving the resolved late cluster. This tests a second fully resolved operating region, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Return to the favorable 60 C regime and make injection 5’s gradient shallower to recover first-pair resolution. This tests whether the higher starting organic fraction can support another maximum-score method with retention near seven minutes.

Test a slightly steeper slope than injection 13 to refine the full-resolution boundary at phi0 = 0.10. The first pair is expected to remain close to R = 1.5 while the last peak elutes slightly earlier.

Test whether a further increase in starting organic fraction, compensated by a shallower gradient, preserves the critical early separation. This extends the window optimization while retaining injection 8 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a slightly cooler, shallower-gradient alternative for full resolution, restoring the low starting organic fraction needed by the first pair. This probes a neighboring temperature setting while keeping the last peak likely below 10 minutes.

Raise injection 16 to 60 C to recover favorable early-pair selectivity and shorten retention. With the maximum score already secured, this tests a method with greater resolution margin while aiming to keep every peak within 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction slightly from injection 17 while keeping its endpoint and duration. This should improve the middle-pair separation and shorten late retention, while the shallower slope may preserve sufficient resolution of the first pair.

Slightly steepen injection 17 to shorten retention while retaining a useful resolution margin for both critical pairs. This refines a maximum-score alternative that is less marginally resolved than the fastest confirmed method, injection 8.

Shorten injection 17’s gradient to eight minutes to reduce retention while targeting full resolution. This matches injection 3’s successful slope, with an endpoint still above the estimated last-peak elution composition.

Shorten injection 18’s gradient by two minutes to reduce retention while using its first-pair resolution margin. The resulting slope is slightly shallower than injection 13’s successful slope, so full resolution is expected with the last peak still inside the gradient.

Lengthen the fastest confirmed maximum-score method by one grid step to test a larger resolution margin without exceeding 10 minutes. Its slope lies between injections 17 and 19, where the two critical pairs were both comfortably resolved.

Raise injection 22’s endpoint by one grid step to shorten retention while preserving full resolution. The resulting slope lies between successful injections 19 and 20, making this a conservative maximum-score refinement.

Use injection 20’s successful slope with a shorter gradient and lower endpoint to test a compact program with more resolution margin than injection 8. The last peak will elute during the hold, so this run checks whether the resulting delay stays below the 10-minute penalty threshold.

Use the final injection for a conservative refinement between the successful slopes of injections 23 and 20, targeting full resolution with the last peak below eight minutes. CRF 1.0 is already secured, and injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
